chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from al-Walid ibn 'Uqba al-Shaybani, from Hamza al-Zayyat, from Humran ibn A'yan, from the one he mentioned, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).

Regarding a people who all drowned, being the family (of the deceased), he said: 'These inherit from these, and these inherit from these, and these do not inherit from what these inherited from these anything, and these do not inherit from what these inherited from these anything.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the family / people of the house

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed when all members of a family die at the same time?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the complex jurisprudence of simultaneous death (*al-ghurqa*), a scenario where the chronological order of death is unknown. It establishes that each deceased individual’s estate is distributed independently to their respective heirs, while explicitly excluding the assets they received from one another to prevent circular inheritance or double-counting within the same event.
